A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mesh tokenization and generation work despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original mesh-generation comparisons, a resampling ablation, compression statistics, and qualitative generation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation experiments and adds non-manifold-data ablations, parameter studies, dataset statistics, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The BFS vertex ordering, matrix compression schemes, component tokens, non-manifold partition rules, progressive resampling, and jointly trained transformer/Michelangelo architecture are retained. Comparing Appendices A-C confirms that the newly emphasized preprocessing and lossless coding are existing components; expanded explanations and pseudocode do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Objaverse/gObjaverse, ShapeNetV2, 3D-FUTURE, and Toys4K, with point-cloud-conditioned generation and the same indirect text/image demonstrations. The added Objaverse subsets and ShapeNetV2 examples extend sampling and analyses within existing coverage, without introducing a distinct domain or conditioning task.

E2.justification: The main generation comparators remain EdgeRunner, TreeMeshGPT, and BPT, with DeepMesh compared qualitatively. The new bits-per-face comparison explicitly substitutes raw xyz coding for VQ-VAE vertex compression, adapting the compression comparators (Appendix D.4). v3 also explicitly compares preprocessing with Libigl in Figure 4.

E3.justification: v3 replaces face-number ratio with bits per face and specifies standardized 7-bit, lossless compression comparisons. It adds fine-tuning on approximately 50k meshes versus 13k manifold meshes, evaluated on 1,000 samples, and window-size studies on approximately 250k Objaverse items. EdgeRunner training now explicitly incorporates the proposed resampling strategy; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained resampling ablation, v3 adds the manifold-only versus mixed-data ablation, matrix-window sensitivity studies, quantization-induced topology statistics, and filtering-coverage analyses. Appendices J-L add real-mesh preprocessing comparisons, component-separation analysis against BPT, and generation failure cases.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v1's checklist asserts statistical reporting but cites only quality metrics. Its removal and v3's added descriptive frequency tables do not constitute a change in uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The main comparison and resampling-ablation scores are replaced: for example, the proposed method's CD changes from 0.079 to 0.025 and NC from 0.708 to 0.792. FR results disappear. New results include 26.652 bits per face, non-manifold-data ablation scores, and Appendix G-H statistics. These are revised or additional reports, not demonstrated gains under verified identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix I.2 adds supporting time and space complexity derivations for vertex ordering and both matrix compressors. The existing stars-and-bars formulation and Euler-based derivation of approximately 2/9 compression are retained without substantive revision.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on eliminating redundant vertex encoding and improving geometric integrity. v3 explicitly broadens the contribution claims to lossless compression assessed in bits per face and online non-manifold processing plus resampling for scalable training without manual curation. Topology preservation becomes the central framing rather than primarily a beneficial property.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of preprocessing's role in data availability, vocabulary-aware compression efficiency, and the computational rationale for matrix-size filtering. Appendices H and L quantify coverage and attribute failures to the 10k-token ceiling and 7-bit quantization. These extend v1's narrower vocabulary-size and filtering limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds tokenization pseudocode, implementation clarifications, a newly disclosed 200-layer limit, processing times of approximately 0.3-0.8 seconds per mesh, and details of component visualization using union-find. Core hardware, optimization, augmentation, and training schedules remain unchanged. The v1 checklist's promised code/checkpoint release statement disappears; the PDFs do not establish an actual availability change.

R1.justification: v3 adds Libigl as an explicit preprocessing reference and develops the distinction between lossless coding and VQ-VAE-based compression. It condenses broader 3D-generation background and removes references such as MVDream and Objaverse-XL. Most central mesh-generation references remain; publication-status updates alone do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method explanations are rewritten. Vertex ordering moves ahead of preprocessing, geometric-property discussion moves into the method section, and experimental subsections are consolidated. The appendices are reorganized and extended, while the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redraws the vertex-ordering and preprocessing diagrams, removes the earlier redundancy illustration, and adds a geometric-property summary, compression and sensitivity tables, and Figures 23-25. Main result tables are restructured. Earlier generation, resampling, and text/image illustrations are reused, while the conference layout relocates and reformats material throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens areas weakly supported in v1: the vocabulary-aware compression comparison addresses compression fairness, while the preprocessing ablation and parameter studies better substantiate practical design choices. Pseudocode, filtering analyses, and concrete failure cases improve transparency and applicability assessment. Unexplained main-score revisions, absent uncertainty estimates, and an inconsistent frequency entry in Table 9 remain weaknesses, but the added validation and documentation provide a substantial net quality gain.
